chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
title: Dakota's husband conducting from behind the curtain; he gives notice
summary: Her husband, a former Dizzy trumpeter, micromanages from backstage, and Malachi quits after the Chicago Roberts Show Lounge engagement.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Anyway, I was very unhappy with the job, because it seemed to be the kind of a job that you could never get settled on. Dakota seemed to be the kind of a person who would pay a lot of compliments about the way you were playing one night, and the next night there would be something wrong with everything. And I think it was out of some frustration that she had with her husband, who I think his name was Talley(?) -- I had formerly known him as Barrymore. He was a trumpet player who had played with Dizzy for a while. And he had married Dakota Staton, and he had taken over as a manager, and he seemed to have some sort of a... He was a little guy and he seemed to have some sort of a Napoleonic complex. He was a tyrant of some kind. He took great pleasure in just trying to manage you all the time. He would

stand backstage when we were playing, he'd stand behind the curtain while you were playing and trying to accompany the artist -- he'd be saying things like "Faster! Louder! Softer!" He'd be conducting from behind the curtain.
So anyway, after the engagement in Chicago, I gave him my notice that I was quitting. And to my amazement, he and Dakota couldn't understand why, and actually seemed regretful that I was leaving.
